question:
Compare the electromagnetic field produced by
(i) a charge at rest,
(ii) a charge moving with uniform velocity, and
(iii) an accelerated charge. Hence explain which of these can produce electromagnetic waves and why.

options.A:
(i) A charge at rest produces both time-varying electric and magnetic fields and emits electromagnetic waves.
(ii) A charge moving uniformly emits waves because it produces a magnetic field.
(iii) An accelerated charge cannot emit waves because its fields are not steady.
Thus, a uniformly moving charge is the only source of electromagnetic waves.
options.B:
(i) A charge at rest produces only an electric field.
(ii) A charge moving uniformly produces electric and magnetic fields.
(iii) An accelerated charge produces no magnetic field.
Both a stationary charge and a uniformly moving charge produce electromagnetic waves because their fields exist in space.
options.C:
(i) A charge at rest produces an electric field but no radiation.
(ii) A charge moving with uniform velocity produces electric and magnetic fields, but does not radiate electromagnetic waves.
(iii) An accelerated charge produces time-varying electric and magnetic fields that sustain each other and propagate through space.
Therefore, only an accelerated charge produces electromagnetic waves.
options.D:
(i) A charge at rest produces no field.
(ii) A charge in uniform motion produces only a magnetic field and therefore radiates.
(iii) An accelerated charge produces only an electric field and cannot radiate.
Thus, any moving charge produces electromagnetic waves.
